newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BLANC MAKES WINNING RETURN TO FRENCH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLANC MAKES WINNING RETURN TO FRENCH LEAGUE.

text.p: France defender Laurent Blanc marked his return to the French league with two goals in six minutes as Marseille came from behind to beat Le Havre 3-1 on Saturday.
Blanc, who signed from Barcelona, equalised Christophe Horlaville's 25th minute opener for Le Havre with a penalty six minutes into the second half after striker Xavier Gravelaine was brought down.
He put the former European champions ahead in the 56th minute direct from a free kick and Gravelaine made it 3-1 with a fine shot from outside the box on the hour.
Marseille coach Rolland Courbis said: "Many of the players began the match very nervously. Laurent's equaliser allowed us to relieve the situation.
"There is everything still to build at OM (Olympique Marseille). For the first day of the championship, what I saw was not at all bad."
Paris St Germain also relied on new signings Florian Maurice and Marco Simone for their first goal in a 2-0 home win over promoted Chateauroux.
France striker Maurice netted a ball from Simone in the 49th minute after the Italian, PSG's biggest ever signing, had been set up by midfielder Jerome Leroy.
Veteran defender Laurent Fournier, also fed by a deft back heel from Leroy, added the second 20 minutes from time when his shot from a tight angle was deflected past the goalkeeper.
Brazil playmaker Leonardo, still being linked with AC Milan, missed a gilt-edged chance after coming on as a second half substitute.
PSG midfielder Vincent Guerin said: "We wanted to start with a win. We also tried to play an attractive game and created several chances. But the team is nowhere near ready."
Both PSG and Marseille, aspirants to the title held by Monaco, made a better start to the season than the champions who went down 1-0 at Bordeaux on Friday.

Lens, who also made telling signings in the off-season with striker Anto Drobnjak joining from Bastia and midfielder Stephane Ziani from Bordeaux, beat 1996 champions Auxerre 3-0 at home -- the best result of the opening weekend.
Auxerre captain Franck Silvestre headed an own goal in the 13th minute, turning a shot by Aboubacar Sankare past goalkeeper Fabien Cool.
Ziani combined with Drobnjak, his former team mate at Bastia, to score the second in the 25th minute after a cross from the left by the Yugoslav international.
Marseille and last season's losing French Cup finalists Guingamp, 3-1 winners against Cannes with two goals from striker Lionel Rouxel, are joint second.
Winger Abdelhajid Tasfaout, who joined Guingamp from Auxerre, was involved in all his new side's goals.

He laid on the first goal for Rouxel in the 18th minute and the second, a penalty, when he was brought down in the 25th. He helped himself to the third when he headed home a free kick from the right one minute before the interval.
Danish veteran Brian Jensen pulled one back for Cannes with a penalty in the 73rd minute.
Metz's new recruit Vladan Lukic scored in their 1-0 win at Lyon, while Bastia defender Sebastien Perez headed the only goal in the Corsican side's 1-0 win at Nantes.
Perez said: "Bastia usually start the season well, but today's obstacle was a big one and we'd never won at Nantes."
